proposals.evidence: Full calati gives Hindi calnā, Mth calab, Bengali calā and Oriya caḷibā with the short-vowel cal stem. These central/eastern simple responses retain that stem with imperative or infinitive endings. Longer auxiliaries and the western cāl/call family, which Turner separately places under *calyati 4721, are not folded into this decision. The link identifies the family while retaining possible regional transfer, explicitly relevant to the eastern Hindi-type forms.

proposals.evidence: Full rātrī gives Kalasha rat, Oriya rāti and the feminine rāt/rāti family throughout central and western Indo-Aryan. These simple night responses preserve that family, including the source’s retroflex t/r and initial reduced vowel. The separate rātra 10700 is the masculine Kashmiri branch, not the comparator used here. Responses containing additional words are excluded.

proposals.citation: CDIAL[6328];webster[Appendix B, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52), item 117, DKS]
proposals.evidence: CDIAL dina supplies regional din “day, daytime”. The same surveyed language independently attests dīn “day” (f_5pvrzs6xrseb2), supporting the local day/sun polysemy rather than choosing a remote sun root by sound alone. The source’s sun gloss, vowel length and dental/retroflex spelling are retained. This identifies the day-word family and leaves possible intra-Indo-Aryan transmission open.
